page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It provides 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core using dedicated CPU allocation on the x86_64 architecture. Cache allocation includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is 16.0 GB, delivering 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate mixed performance across differing workload types. Single-core processing is solid, demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score in the top 25% (2923.69) and an average Geekbench single-core score of 1645.0. However, multi-threaded metrics scale lower due to the 4-vCPU limit, with stress-ng multi-core (5862.86) and Geekbench multi-core (3752.0) ranking in the bottom 25%. Instruction support includes AES, SHA-NI, and standard AVX, though advanced extensions like AVX-512 and AMX are absent. Large block memory read and write bandwidth hold steady at 51.54 GB/sec and 38.79 GB/sec respectively.

With a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the server maintains adequate RAM density for small-scale applications, though the absence of bundled local NVMe storage requires external persistent disks. Given its strong single-thread performance alongside lower multi-threaded throughput, c2d-standard-4 is primarily suited for general web serving, single-threaded batch processing, lightweight CI/CD tasks, and low-scale application backends rather than dense parallel computing or I/O-heavy database workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-4 is a compute-optimized instance providing 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of memory on an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, it offers dedicated CPU allocation with a 32 MB L3 cache. The instance excludes bundled local storage and accelerators. In benchmark testing, it delivers strong single-core CPU execution, achieving a top 25% stress-ng single-core result of 2923.69, while multi-core metrics like Geekbench multi-core (3752.0) and parallel compiling reflect lower throughput relative to larger cloud nodes. Memory bandwidth reaches 51.54 GB/sec for uncached reads and 38.79 GB/sec for writes. The instance is suitable for entry-level computational tasks, single-threaded processing, and basic web serving where high core density is unnecessary.
